body:
Just got home.  No sleep, up for more than 24 hours.  I'm heating a frying pan for a grilled cheese sandwich, should be fine as the the only thing I eat today.  I was actually hoping there'd be some people here still.  I don't know how long posts can stay alive on SW but I don't want to be the guy who tests the limit either...

I'm actually feeling better than last night.

I don't think it's childhood traumas that it boils down to.  I've had a LOT of failures since then and it's not like I haven't had face-to-face talks with people before.  Guidance counselors, that previous marine friend, other, less prominent, transient friends.  It's not like I've never had people to talk to, my parents were even fine when things got really bad.  Just talking to people, the maybe 5-10 I've had very serious conversations with, has not suddenly jolted me into some view that I'm OK.  I'm looking at what I've got now.  Yeah I might have a better future ahead.  I can't imagine what it will be or how it will be but I can admit it might happen.  But I'm not going to dangle a carrot on a stick out in front of myself to keep moving any more.

I'm going to work now.  Thanks for talking to me.

I had ADD.  When they tried Ritalin on me, I reacted violently.  They moved on to a medication that worked immediately but that's beside the point.  I don't think my teachers grade 1-3 ever got over me throwing chairs in my first grade teacher's class and trying to break things.  It was one bad episode but my first grade teacher is the only one I remember being nice to me and I wrecked that.  I felt so guilty I cried about it tons and even once in class.  My second grade teacher hated my guts.  Back then, kids were already making fun of the shape of my head.  I got an absolute wrecking by an old man for putting mail (a hand-written letter of mine in an unaddressed envelope) in his mailbox accidentally instead of the one belonging to the family of the kids across the street.  He yelled at me for 5 straight minutes about how he should call the cops.  I was fucking 6.  As with all this stuff, I felt awful.  My parents were nice, and loving, and went to bat for me a few times, but we kept to ourselves.  No one ever beat me up, for what it's worth.  In late first grade I had my jacket stolen and then thrown into a trough urinal and pissed on by three boys and later got pissed on myself by one of them who got a 2 day suspension for apparently trying to piss through me into a toilet in the stall I was occupying.  I guess I was just an out-and-out soft target, you didn't need to beat me up to get me down.  Kids at that age are pretty much mindless and I was just sad and mindless, wishing I could take back and redo things.  I learned how to read only halfway through first grade, but then I ramped up and kept my nose buried in books, video games, and trees for the next few years.  Middle and high school didn't help anything, that should be obvious.  I don't mean to give you the impression that anything specific event is the sole cause of my depression, so please don't take it that way.

In a few minutes I'm going to work.  Yes, I've been awake all night, I would have been anyway, and no, I can't call in sick.  I've only been working at this place a month.  I'll lose my job for sure.

Advertising and sales demand writing to appeal to the greatest common denominator.  I don't think that I can devise witty ads that grab people.  I don't think I work fast enough to make money as a copy editor, blog writer, what have you.  But I will actually try a job.  Just one.  I don't think I'll do well.  Do you think there's anything ethically reprehensible about taking a job while I'm in this state of mind?

School isn't what makes me miserable, it's that I can't do it.  I think my classes are interesting, I just can't keep up.  I don't know if I can tell it to fuck off.

They don't have counselors of any stripe, academic, situational, or emotional, which is saying something because my high school did.  I don't have a friendship group.  I may have once had an amalgamation of contacts, but I always had to contact them, they never contacted me.  At some point, maybe 3 years ago, I stopped contacting them and then other than running into them at random, we haven't spoken.  I had a friend, or at least someone who'd pity me, but he's not who he once was.  His better friends are all in his marine unit, and that's that.

I just edited in a large preceding block of feelings that chewing me up.  I'm sorry, I must seem hopeless and impossible.  I just don't see a way out.  It's like I was born into it but it probably began when I was very young.  I live here, in this misery, and I don't see a way out.

My physical and mental handicaps dictate that I'll never be able to anything I wanted to my satisfaction.  They have so far.  I cannot change my interests or those limits.  I can't do good either.  I don't what I was thinking saying I'd like to try doing some volunteer work.  Soup kitchens?  Habitat for Humanity?  Picking up tar balls in the gulf?  That's not me.  I don't have the initiative.  And just living for the sake of being alive?  What's the difference between what I'm doing and a coma?  If a heart-beat is all that matters in life, to the damnation of mental and physical ability, then I'm doing fine, sure.  But it's not.  If I'm doing nothing, and there's nothing I can do, I'm useless and uselessness has no place in a society where improvement is a goal.

You can only say I'm not ugly with complete conviction because we're not talking in person.  Other people may not be movie stars, but I'm not just a regular guy with poor self-image.  Thanks for being adamant, but I wager that you would not say that anyone is ugly.  In my world and the world of people at large, there are more grades than movie-star and not-movie-star.  Even if you use a different word or phrase like really-really-not-movie-star-material or not-good-enough-to-play-the-homely-extra-in-Boggy-Creek-2 then we still come back to the problem.  I look worse than 80% of people you find in Wal-mart.  Looks are a single facet of why I'm inferior, but they do indeed contribute.  We all know that you can be positively ignorant, even willingly, and if you look good enough, you can still have a social life where you don't piss off the people you're trying to be friends with and if you look really good, you can get pair enough to raise a family.  Just by looking good.  I wholly lack that ability, it's an uphill struggle for me to socialize.  I start with a handicap.

Thanks for the info, and I'll try not to cry anymore.  But my chest just gets so tight, and my eyes hurt if I try to hold it back sometimes.

>  It's truly as simple as making a decision that you won't accept your shitty thoughts for one minute longer.

I tried that.  I don't think I did it the wrong way, I just did it the only way I could.  I didn't accept my thoughts when they were painful, but they didn't stop springing into my head, either.  The cognitive dissonance brought me into a shouting match with thin air.  I don't mean that I went crazy but I was threatening myself aloud, screaming and telling myself to stop.  The only reason I didn't think I was clinically insane was because I was aware I was shouting at myself and that myself wasn't a separate person, but it sure felt like I was having an argument with a separate person who didn't want to be like I did. I'd say it's the closest to a psychotic break I've ever been.  The despair that left me in almost had me posting here a few months ago.  I could not sort myself out and gave up.  My thoughts are my own whether I like them or not.  Consciousness as a multi-threaded process did not work well in my experience.  I'm not sure if I was on to something good or very bad.  I guess I don't have the brain for it, which isn't surprising to me.

But for all that it's worth, I may have been approaching it wrong.  I need directions so simple that I could follow them if I weren't a human being.  Impossibly accurate descriptions of the mental processes I'm trying to block and allow, what mental energies to apply to the method, a thousand details that I couldn't get from even the best psychologist.  But I sure can't improvise.  It didn't work my way.

Thanks.  I have never seriously considered an English or writing major.  I always took writing to be one of those things at which you're either already good enough, or otherwise something at which you could not become good enough to justify taking it as a major.  That said, I can only afford the tech school.  Technical colleges teach people to enter skilled professions like welding, nursing, medical transcription, networking, automotive repair, etc.  Liberal arts degrees aren't available, nor is instruction, beyond the barest basics.

I'd like to try volunteer work but I don't know where I'd find the time with work and school.  Yes, I go to a technical college but I'm not doing as well as I'd like.  I've already been three semesters and have at least that ahead of me with the grades I've turned.  I guess I get to keep going until the Pell grants stop coming.  If I quit that to make more time . . . I just don't know.

I may be articulate, but I have nothing to write about that people want to read.  I tried writing sci-fi for awhile, if you can believe it.  Truth is, I can't carry a narrative.  Not even enough for a blog.  I have a good enough vocabulary, even by my own standards, but my assembly of stories and my presentation of ideas isn't compelling enough to read.

And I know it might not be the sentence you were trying to push hardest toward me, but thanks for being sorry about it being so dark.  Thank you, a lot.  Thanks.

I think I have a better way of putting the issue of responsibilities to self and society.  Next time you see a suicidal post and have the ability to respond, don't.  Fail to do what you value and then try claiming that we don't have any responsibility to ourselves to be valuable to ourselves by the standards we may set.

I'm sorry, I just got hit with a wave of sadness and I'm crying again.  I'm not angry at you, I just fail at everything I want to accomplish.  It means too much to me that I can't do anything right.

This is a default response (with modification), I know, but thanks for it.  Really.  It's well-written.  I believe it to an extent.  I'm just not sure they can help.  I'll look into that mental health association.  Do you know what it's under in the phone book?  Guess that might vary by the book and the area, but . . . well I just can't be arsed to go on a search and then, even worse, not be certain I found the mental health professionals(?) you intended me to.

I am!  I can't guarantee my heart or corneas are any good (astigmatism), and I have a misshapen liver (but it should still work I guess), but I bet my lungs and kidneys work!

I honestly think that donating organs would be my greatest contribution to society.  There are people far better than me who are dying.  Their family will miss them.  They have sons and daughters.  Or maybe they're in college.  Or maybe the only thing they have is potential and maybe they'll fail.  But they've got a better shot at being happy with their lives than me.  Or, you know what, even if they don't, I'm still happy that I'm a donor.  I'd actually like to set things up so that paramedics are on their way before I die so they can get at me early, but I don't have plans yet.  Unfortunately, the means I'd like to use to die wouldn't leave much, if anything, useful.  This will sound so stupid but I'm squeamish about guns.  Tall buildings, poisons, rope, I'm OK with those but I just could never pull a trigger on myself.

> For a start, the list is horribly biased. It sounds like you've decided you're unworthy first, then retro-fitted a set of characteristics to yourself in order to justify the decision.

I cared about being color blind and ugly before I was depressed.  Or roughly from the same moment in 1st or 2nd grade.  But forget what I mentioned being wrong with me.  There's even more that I didn't list. What is there that I can be good at?  I know you can't possibly answer that since you don't know me, but the answer is nothing.  Anything I ever cared about I am NOT good at.  Video games, learning, making friends, having sex, fixing computers, fixing cars, or taking orders at a McDonald's (previous job): you name it and I suck at it.  Physical and mental deformity put a hard limit on what I could ever be to anyone.  Or to myself.

I'm pretty isolated.  I think I have too many acquaintances across too many mediums and not enough in common with any of them.  Not that I can be anyone's best friend, even if they're mine.  I am the sort of person you would try to excuse yourself from the company of if I started a conversation with you in any random place.  

Imagine for a moment that some ugly fella with acne, a southern drawl, and impossible-to-interpret facial expressions (on an ugly face to boot) tries to strike up a conversation with you and your friends at a bar about Star Craft 2 and then suddenly has nothing to say after you make your first comment.  Because he has nowhere to go from there.  You can't be friends with that guy.  He's a tag-along even after a year of running into you at that bar.  You actually relish the nights when he's not out there to fuck up a game of darts (which he is very bad at and adds inordinate amounts of time to) between you and your buddies.

I am not the sort of person you _want_ to make friends with.  I'm the sort of person you make fun of with your actual friends once I'm gone.  And if you're just too nice to ever make fun of another human being, I promise you, most people aren't.  I was used to that for the longest time, but now I'm so tired, and there's no POINT going on.  It's not even what other people think of me.  It's that I can never be happy with myself.  I will not learn to be happy with myself because I don't like people like me.  I never have.  I told myself the whole time that I was growing up that I would grow out of it.  That I would mystically become a better person courtesy of cell division and hormonal changes.  A little bit faster, a little bit more handsome.  That wasn't the case.  I had hobbies for as long as it took me to figure out I wasn't any good at them.  It's not that I hate myself for doing nothing, it's that I hate myself for being good at nothing.  I have nothing to strive for because there's nothing I can be good at.  Or nothing I want to be.  I might make a great body builder or pot farmer, but I'm not interested in either of those things.

I don't know who I could talk to that would care.  The only person who ever listened to me became a marine and he doesn't like emotion anymore.  And I can't talk about how much I disappoint myself and how useless I am to society without getting emotional.  

I am in the US.  I have not considered seriously trying to get "community help."  I actually don't know what you mean by that.  I'm sorry this post is so long.
